(a) to (c) The Hallmarking Scheme of Gold Jewellery was launched 
by Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) in April, 2000, on the request of 
Reserve Bank of India, Government of India. The principal objectives of 
the Hallmarking Scheme are to ensure that the common consumer is 
assured of the purity of gold jewellery purchased by him. Hallmarking 
Scheme is voluntary in nature and is being operated under the BIS Act, 
1986. As per the scheme, licence is  granted to jeweller (retailer/ 
manufacturer/wholesaler), after ensu ring that all the requirements of 
Indian Standard IS: 1417 for purity are being complied with.

Telephone Directory for Delhi and Mumbai 
* 342. SHRI DINESH TRIVEDI  :† 
          SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: 
WILL THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state : 
(a) whether it is a fact that in spite of a large number of changes in 
telephone numbers in Mumbai, Delhi and all metros and the directive of 
the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India to make directories available to the 
telephone subscribers annually, the main telephone directories for Delhi 
and Mumbai have not been published since 1999 and 2000 respectively; 
(b) what steps MTNL has taken to ensure that telephone directories 
are made available to the subscriber s of Delhi and Mumbai in time on a 
regular basis; and 
†The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri Dinesh 
Trivedi. 
9 

RAJYA SABHA [ 14 August, 2003] 
(c) whether Government have examined the feasibility of bringing 
out the directories by fixed dates? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI ARUN SHOUR IE): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid 
on the table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) Sir, in MTNL, Delhi, tne last issue of directory was published 
in 2000. In MTNL Mumbai, the last main directory was published in 
1999. The supplement 2001 has also been printed and distributed to 
subscribers in 2002 by MTNL Mumbai. 
In MTNL Delhi and Mumbai, tenders for six year period, are now 
being processed for bringing out directories every two years (main 
directory every alternate year and in the intervening period a 
supplementary directory). 
Meanwhile steps have been taken to make information available, 
which is normally contained in the printed directory, in other formats:- 
(i) IN CD ROM (priced concessionally at Rs. 50/-), which is updated 
at least once in a year and is av ailable at all Customer Service 
Centre/Sanchar Haat of MTNL. 
(ii) On internet website of MTNL, (www. mtnl.net.in) which is updated 
online. 
(iii) Toll-free Directory Information Service through '197'. 
According to information available, there is no directive of the Hon. 
Supreme Court of India to make directories available to the telephone 
subscribers annually. However, the guidelines of Department of Telecom, 
which are applicable to MTNL do provide that telephone directories be 
printed every alternative year an d in the intervening period, a 
supplementary directory be printed and made available to subscribers. 
SHRI DINESH TRIVEDI: Sir, at the outset, although this question 
relates to telephone directories in Delhi and Mumbai, yet, I am sure, 
the hon. Minister and yourself would appreciate that a similar situation 
is prevalent all over the country. The statement of the hon. Minister has 
two aspects. The first aspect does  answer my question. "Yes, on 
publication of directories, a backlog of three or four years is there." 
10 

[14 August, 2003] RAJYA SABHA 
And the second aspect of the statem ent talks of the sources where we 
can get the information updated. Sir, today, it is all the more required; 
every day the telephone numbers are changing. Whether two is added 
or five is subtracted, or it is becoming an eight-digit number, it is a 
constant change. You will appreciate that the telephone directories 
are not only the source for telephone numbers, but we look into the 
telephone directory for several other reasons as well, like, finding out 
addresses and things like that. So, Sir, my supplementary is: Why is it 
that the supply of telephone directories has been delayed by three 
years or so? No. 2: Would you consider bringing it every six months 
instead of one year? And, the second part of it is, when you talk about 
getting the information in CD ROM, I would like to know how many 
citizens of this country, who have telephones, have a computer also. 
SHRI ARUN SHOURIE: Sir, it is a very important supplementary. It 
is true that there are delays of tw o to three years in the production of 
directories. This delay used to be five years; it has now cut down to two 
to three years. In Delhi, the direct ory was printed last in 1999, and its 
supplement was printed in the year 2000. In Mumbai, it was printed in 
2000 and the supplement was printed in 2001. Under the existing 
guidelines, the main directory has to be published every second year 
that is, the alternate year, and in the meantime, a supplement has to be 
brought out. The problem is arising because of several reasons. One of 
the reasons, I think, is the cost of the directory. Now, it is in four volumes, 
and each time it is printed, it costs about Rs. 60 crores. Now, for instance, 
for Delhi, the contract has just been finalised, and it is going to cost the 
MTNL, for Delhi and Mumbai, a sum of  Rs. 328 crores. And, as per a 
judgement of the Chennai High Court in 1992, these will have to be given 
free. They had said, "You give them free till you print a new one." But, 
since 1992, no Government has been able to levy even a nominal charge 
on this. Each directory's production is costing Rs. 161—165. Now, there 
are several solutions to this. One of the solutions is, a tender-has been 
floated in February, 2003, for MTNL, and we hope to finalise it this month. 
And, by the end of the year, in both  cases, certainly in Delhi, a new 
directory will be available. Also, the order last time was for 16 lakh copies. 
But a large number of copies remained unpicked because actually now, 
the people don't want to pick up the four volume of the directory. Trivediji 
was right in saying that the people need the directory. But we have found

that the directories are not being picked up, and in the first two years, 
nearly 70 per cent of th e customers did not pick up their directories. 
The order this time is for 10 lakh copies. If more need arises, we will 
order for more. There are several step s which can be taken. I will explain 
more when the other Members put their supplementaries. 
SHRI DINESH TRIVEDI: It is all the more the reason why the MTNL 
should come up and update it at th e earliest. Earlier, when these 
guidelines were laid down, It was a monopoly. Now the private sector 
also has come into play. Sir, the hon. Minister has referred to the Chennai

Today, the Yellow Pages are being used for commercial purposes. I 
am sure, the hon. Minister who is very dynamic, can consider getting 
more advertisements in the 'yellow pages' part, and give it to the people 
free of cost, as it had always been done in the past. Will the hon. Minister 
consider this suggestion? 
SHRI ARUN SHOURIE: Mr. Chairman, Sir, this is a very important 
suggestion. As you know, earlier, the yellow pages used to be printed as 
a part of the directory. Then, the Tata Press decided to print the Yellow 
Pages on its own, and distribute the Yellow Pages free of cost. Then, the 
MTNL had protested in this case, and TATAs had taken it to the Supreme 
Court. In 1995, the Supreme Court said that they could also print. 
Unfortunately, in my view, the decision was taken .that, then, the MTNL 
and the BSNL will not print their own Yellow Pages. This was not 
necessary. The Supreme Court, Mr. Trivedi has implied, did not bar the 
MTNL from doing this. I will be working with the MTNL to see as to why 
they do not want to enter into this commercial activity and thereby make 
some profits; distribute the 'yellow pages' free; and subsidise the directory 
by some way. 
Secondly, the hon. Member is right  that the main directory itself 
should be able to have some advertisements. This is the practice, which 
is prevalent all over the world. It helps in subsidising the cost of production 
of directories. We will be considering this suggestion. 
Sir, as Mr. Trivedi had asked as to how many people have computers, 
with your permission, I would just like to mention that the MTNL—

DR. A. K. PATEL: Mr. Chairman, Sir, the Ahmedabad Directory had 
not been published since 1997. I would like to know from the hon. 
Minister when he is going to publish it. 
SHRI ARUN SHOURIE: Sir, with your permission, I would try to 
explain as to what really happened in this case. It is right that the 
contract for printing the Ahmedabad Directory was given in 1994, and 
it was printed in 1997 for the year 1995-96. Then, a judgement came 
from the Madras High Court that the directories must be distributed 
free of cost. In 1995, there was another judgement that the Yellow 
Pages can be printed by TATAs on their own, and distributed free. The 
result was that the person, who had taken the contract for printing the 
Ahmedabad Directory, said, "I cannot print dirctories from 1998 
onwards because it will not be econo mic." He refused to print the 1998- 
99 directories at old rates. Then, th e district authority of the BSNL 
took the matter to the court that the contractor must honour his contract. 
It went to Arbitrator. The Arbitrator awarded in the favour of contractor. 
The Ahmedabad Telephone District, then, went to the City Civil Court 
to have the Arbitrator's award set aside. The contractor, then, moved 
to the High Court, which went in his favour. 
The BSNL then moved the Supreme Court. Meanwhile, a second 
tender was floated, and, unfortunately, the same contractor became L1. 
Under the CVC rules, you have to award the contract to the same person.

he is in a dispute and as he has defaulted in the previous contract, do not 
award him the contract." Therefore, th is contract was allowed to lapse. 
This tender was allowed to lapse, and a third tender was floated and this 
person was not permitted to bid. He, therefore, moved the Delhi High 
Court and he obtained a stay. Now, what has happened is that an out-of- 
Court settlement has been arrived at, and all cases have been withdrawn 
by the third parties. He will forgo the award of the arbitrator, and he will 
print the directory in this financial year for Ahmedabad at the second 
tender rate which he had refused when he was the LI. If he does not 
print, the security deposit of five per cent of the tender will be forfeited. 
...(Interruptions)...And, then, again, he might go to the court. But, Sir, I 
hope, in this financial year, we will be able to print it again.

Production of sugar 
*344. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI BARUPAL: 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether sugar season showed an  excess of sugar production in 
2002-03 (October—September); 
(b) if so, what was the total sugar production in 2002-03; 
(c) whether in the sugar season of 2003-04, the assessment up-till 
nine months show that the 200 lakh tonnes mark has been crossed; 
(d) if so, whether the excess pro duction of sugar would create a 
problem in the country; 
(e) whether Government are considering to export more and more 
sugar during this year; 
(f) if so, the efforts being made; and 
(g) whether more export orders have been obtained? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) to (g) Sugar production 
during the current 2002- 2003 (October—September) sugar season is 
estimated at about 200 lakh tonnes, as against 185.25 lakh tonnes 
during the 2001-2002 sugar season. As on 7th July, 2003, the total 
production during the 2002-2003 season was 198'.65 lakh tonnes 
(provisional). The sugar season 2003-2004 (October—September) has 
yet to commence. 
2. Sugar is exported under Open General Licence (OGL) and private 
parties/sugar mills export the same as per commercial judgement. 
The measures taken to promote the exports of sugar include: 
(i)  Quantitative restriction on export of sugar has been removed. 
(ii) Sugar meant for exports is exempted from the levy obligation. 
(iii) The quantity of sugar released for export is treated as advance 
freesale release to be adjusted in the freesale stocks of the 
sugar factories after a period of 18 months.

(iv) Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB) at the rate of 4% of the 
FOB value of export of sugar has been allowed. 
(v) The Sugar Development Fund Act, 1982 has been amended in 
order, inter alia, to utilize the Sugar Development Fund for 
defraying expenditure on internal transport charges and 
neutralization of ocean freight disadvantage to the sugar factories 
on export shipments of sugar. 
3. During the financial year 2002-2003, the exports of sugar have 
amounted to approximately 14.70 lakh tonnes.

Disparity in minimum wage 
*347. DR. ABRAR AHMED: 
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: 
Will the Minister of LABOUR be pleased to state : 
(a) whether there is any disparity in rates of minimum wage in 
various regions of the country; if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the reasons for variation from region to region; and 
25 

RAJYA SABHA [14 August, 2003] 
(c) the steps being taken to bring in regional uniformity in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR (SHRI SAHIB SINGH VERMA): (a) 
and (b) Yes, Sir. There is disparity in rates of minimum wages in various 
regions of the country, which is due to differences in socio-economic 
and agro-climatic conditions, prices of essential commodities, paying 
capacity, productivity and local conditions influencing the wage rate. 
The regional disparity in minimum wages is also attributed to the fact 
that both the Central and State Governments are the appropriate 
Government to fix, revise and enforce minimum wages in scheduled 
employments in their respective jurisdictions under the Minimum Wages 
Act, 1948. 
(c) In order to minimize the disparity in minimum wages in various 
regions of the country, the Central Government has issued guidelines 
for setting up Regional Minimum Wages Advisory Committees. In order 
to bring in uniformity in minimum wages, the Central Government mooted 
the concept of a national floor level minimum wage and fixed it at 
Rs. 35/- per day inl996 based on the recommendations of the National 
Commission on Rural Labour (1991) and subsequent rise in the price 
level. The national floor level wage is periodically revised based on the 
basis of increase in the Consumer Price Index. It was last revised to 
Rs. 50/- per day w.e.f. 1.9.2002. The States/UTs have been requested 
from time to time to ensure that the minimum wage in none of their 
scheduled employments is below the national floor level wage.

Statement 
The Vision, Objectives and Strate gy for supporting Electronics/IT 
hardware manufacturing as outlined in the Draft Paper on National 
Electronics/IT Hardware Manufacturing Policy are as follows:— 
Vision 
To make India one of the key play ers in the global electronics/IT 
Hardware — manufacturing sector and integrate with the global value- 
added-chain. 
Objectives 
Growth of Electronics/IT Hardware industry in India has not been 
consistent with the market potential.  The objectives of the strategy 
in supporting/encouraging hardware manufacturing would thus be as 
follows:— 
(a) Spurring the Domestic demand; 
(b) Making Indian Electronics/IT Hardware Sector globally 
competitive; 
(c) Facilitating the industry for addressing global markets; 
(d) Facilitate formation of catalysts for growth of the industry;

(f) Focus on value-added products; 
(g) Reducing dependence on imports;

Strategy for Supporting Electronics/IT Hardware Manufacturing 
The strategy for supporting/encouraging manufacture of hardware in 
India is aimed at providing a fertile business ambience in which the 
investments would flourish and making the industry globally competitive. 
The measures proposed in this direction and to achieve the objectives 
are as follows:— 
Tariff Policy 
Reduction of customs duty to zero% on all the raw materials and 
inputs, capital goods, abolition of SAD, sales tax @ 4%, excise duty 
@8% etc. 
Exim Policy 
Unification of investments for manufacturing for domestic and

*352. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: 
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO : 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state : 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided that the unit 
size of the future power reactors in the country be increased to 700 MW 
capacity instead of 250 MW or 540 MW capacity; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) what important project implementation strategies have been 
adopted by the Nuclear Power Corp oration of India to reduce the 
construction period of atomic plants in India? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC 
ENERGY (SHRI SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) and (b) Pressurised 
Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) beyond those presently under 
construction (unit sizes of 220 MWe and 540 MWe) are planned to be 
of 700 MWe unit size, based on scaling up of 540 MWe unit design. 
The reactor core in 700 MWe design is same as in 540 MWe and only 
a few small changes have been made  in other nuclear systems. Design 
and development works on 700 MWe PHWRs are in an advanced stage. 
(c) Strategies being adopted in the construction of projects under 
construction for reducing construction time are as follows: 
Completion of pre-project activities in design and development of 
site infrastructure before commencing the construction of the project. 
Timely manufacture of components/equipment in the context of 
the experience gained in the field. 
Adopting the concept of large supply-cum-erection packages to 
the extent feasible. 
Increased use of automation in the construction. 
Strengthening project management techniques and monitoring 
mechanism for controlling schedule.

*358. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY:

 49

the targeted employment opportunities have been identified;

employment opportunities in the country?

have already been published by the Planning Commission.

under the Tenth Plan, Planning Commission has set up a Task Force on 
formulation of State level employment strategy, monitoring employment 
generation at State level and implementation of employment related 
programmes and policies in the Tenth Plan by the State Governments.

(b) whether Government have examined the feasibility of providing 
technologies having low running cost, minimum maintenance, cheap and 
reliable in rural and remote areas; and

service providers. After the formation of BSNL in October, 2000, the

Public Telephones (VPTs). As a result of this study, WLL (Wireless in

under the PMRY in the State of Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details thereof for the last three years, year-wise and

(c) the reasons for such huge gaps; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF AGRO AND RURAL 
INDUSTRIES(SHRI SANGHPRIYAGAUTAM):(a)and(b)Yes, Sir. Based 
on the reports received from the St ate Government, a Statement showing 
bank-wise (both public and private sector banks), details of persons

there is going to be a gap between the number of applications 
recommended to banks and actual disbursement made by the banks. 
The other reasons reported by the State Government and the Reserve 
Bank of India are delay in completing pre-disbursement formalities by 
the applicants and arranging training for applicants before disbursement 
of loans, non-adherence to the quarterly schedule of sponsoring and 
disbursement of applications by the implementing agencies, 
unsatisfactory recovery of loan overdues, sponsoring of non-viable 
projects by the District Task Force Committees, etc.

implementing agencies to adhere to the time frame for disposing off the 
applications, banks have been instructed to impart necessary sensitisation 
programmes for the branch level officials to bring attitudinal changes 
etc. The State Government has taken steps like updating of viable project 
profiles, regular review and monitoring  of the performance of the Scheme 
at Mandal level, District & State level, opening of Entrepreneurs Guidance

fraudulently or by his wilful act or default. This expemption is not absolute.

Recommendations made by "High level Committee on long-term 
grain policy" 
2605. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH :Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state : 
(a) the status report of implementation by Government as on date, 
with regard to various recommendations and proposals as made through 
a report by the "High level Committee on long-term grain policy", July 
2002; and 
(b) what remedial measures are being taken by Government towards 
greater production and proper security of Food Distribution in view of the 
report having shown at all India level, much decrease in food production, 
area of cultivation and yield per hectare from 1999 which is a warning 
signal for a rapid negative growth of production? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION ( SHRI SUBHASH 
MAHARIA : (a) Government has examined the major recommendations 
121 

RAJYA SABHA [ 14 August, 2003 ] 
made by the High Level Committee on Long Term Grain Policy (HLC) 
constituted under the Chairmanship of Prof. Abhijit Sen. 
The action taken with regard to the main recommendations of the 
HLC are as under:— 
(i) The HLC has made several recommendations with regard to the 
Fixing of the Minimum Support Prices of foodgrains. The 
Government has, however, decided that the present Minimum 
Support Price Regime should continue. 
(ii) With regard to the recommendation of the HLC for introduction 
of a universal Public-Distribution System (PDS) with uniform 
Central Issue Prices (CIPs). It is felt by the Government that 
the targeted PDS was introduced in June, 1997 with a view to 
target the unprivileged sections  of society, as the earlier 
universal PDS did not adequately focus on the poor and hungry 
and had an urban bias. Under the TPDS, the families Below the 
Poverty Line (BFL) have been identified and foodgrains are 
supplied to the BPL families at highly subsidized rates at less 
than 50% of the economic cost at the scale of 35 Kg. per family 
per month. The introduction of a universal PDS will result in the 
PDS losing its focus on meeting the needs of the poor. 
(iii) The HLC has recommended that for an effective foodgrains 
management system, it is necessary to liquidate the excess 
accumulation of stocks. To achieve this, several measures have 
been taken as a result of which stocks have reduced from 630 
lakh tonnes as on 1st July, 2002 to 352 lakh tonnes as on 
1st July, 2003. 
(iv) The HLC also recommended disposal of old stocks and stock 
procured under relaxed quality st ocks. As a result of measures 
taken for disposal of such stocks, over 80% of current stocks 
are less than 2 years old. 
(v) As recommended by the HLC, the coverage of households has 
been increased by an additional 50 lakh persons with focus on 
the destitute population under Antyodaya Anna Yojana. 
122 

[ 14 August, 2003 ] RAJYA  SABH A 
(vi) The allocation under the Sampoorna Gramin RojgarYojana(SGRY) 
and Special Component'of the SGRY scheme has been 
considerably enhanced as recommended by the HLC. 
(vii) To improve functioning of the PDS instructions have already been 
issued for strict implementation of PDS Control Order to ensure 
greater transparency in the working of the PDS and reduction in 
the diversion of foodgrains under the PDS. Guidelines have been 
issued for the involvement of the Panchayat: Raj Institutions in 
the implementation of the TPDS. 
(b) The agricultural production in the country shows a long term upward 
trend, albeit with fluctuations due to weather aberrations. A major factor 
for sustaining this growth, especially in foodgrains production, has been 
the procurement policy under Minimum Support Price operations. 
Government is also implementing the following schemes to further improve 
the production of cereals :— 
(i)   Integrated Cereals Development Programme in Rice Based 
Cropping Systems Areas (ICDP-Rice) 
(ii)   Integrated Cereals Deve lopment Programme in Wheat Based 
Cropping System Areas (ICDP-Wheat) 
(iii) Integrated Cereals Developm ent Programme in Coarse Cereals 
Based Cropping System Areas (ICDP-Coarse Cereals) 
From October, 2002 these schemes have heen subsumed under the 
Macro Management Programme with a view to provide flexibility to the 
States according to regionally differe ntiated needs of the States. As a 
new initiative, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme on "On Farm Water 
Management for Increasing Crop Production in Eastern India" has been 
launched on 19th March, 2002 for the year 2001-02 and for the Tenth 
Five Year Plan, the objective of the scheme is to exploit the ground/ 
surface water, efficient water utilization and management for increasing 
crop production in Eastern India. 
The schemes undertaken to increase production of cereals, as 
detailed, the decision to continue with the present procurement regime 
and the actions taken to expand the scope and allocation of foodgrains 
under various welfare schemes of the Government will ensure food 
security in the country.

Indo-China Joint Working Group 
 † 2654. SHRI LAJPAT RAI: 
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: 
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state : 
(a) whether it is a fact that a joint working group was constituted in 
the year 1998 to resolve the disputes between India and China; 
(b)if so, the number of meetings held so far of the said group; 
(c) the details of various disputes discussed in these 
meetings; and 
(d) whether any of them has been sorted out, so far? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI VINOD KHANNA): (a) to (d) The India-China Joint Working 
Group (JWG) on the Boundary Question was constituted in 1988. It 
has met 14 times. The 14th meeting of the JWG was held in New Delhi 
on 21st November, 2002. 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi 
165 

RAJYA SABHA [14 August, 2003] 
India and China seek a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable 
settlement of the boundary question through peaceful consultations. 
They signed an agreement on the Maintenance of Peace and Tranquility 
along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the India-China Border Areas 
in 1993 and a second agreement on Confidence Building Measures in 
the Military Field along the Line of Actual Control in the India-China 
Border Areas in 1996. These two Agreements provide an institutional 
framework for the maintenance of peace and tranquility in the border 
areas. The process of clarification of the LAC has started within existing 
mechanisms. Maps of the LAC in the Middle Sector have been 
exchanged. Discussions have commenced on clarification of the LAC in 
the Western Sector of the India-China boundary 
During the 14th meeting of the JWG, both sides reviewed the 
ongoing process of LAC clarification. They also continued discussions 
on further confidence Building M easures. Both sides agreed, inter alia, 
on the need to substantially enhance trade and economic relations, 
cultural and people-to-people exchanges. Both sides also reviewed 
the functioning of the existing dialogue mechanisms, such as on counter 
terrorism and security, and agreed to establish a dialogue mechanism 
between the two Foreign Offices on policy planning . Regional and 
international issues were also discussed.

Gloomy picture of Indian economy 
2677. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH : Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state :

has recently painted a gloom and doom picture of Indian economy; 
(b) if so, the detail of their findings; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRI SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) and (b) The World Bank in 
its development policy review entitled 'India: Sustaining Reform, 
Reducing Poverty' released on July 14, 2003, while acknowledging that 
India's growth over the past two decades has been one of the world's 
highest among large countries, has expressed concern over the 
deterioration in the fiscal position of the Centre and States. The Review

composition has limited the prosp ect for accelerating growth and

deficit and promoting investment for productive purposes. Fiscal 
consolidation is one of the five prio rities addressed in the Union Budget 
for 2003-04. The Budget has proposed a number of initiatives, such as, 
promoting infrastructure development by leveraging public money through 
private sector participation, promoting private investment and measures 
aimed at fiscal consolid ation. These initiatives, inter alia, are expected 
to have a positive influence on the growth of the economy.

Steps to develop and boost SSI 
2692. PROF M. SANKARALINGAM: Will the Minister of SMALL 
SCALE INDUSTRIES be pleased to state : 
(a) the steps taken to develop and boost the SSIs during the last four 
years; 
(b) the number of persons employed in SSI during the said period; 
and 
(c) the number of SSIs set up in the country during the last four 
years, State-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES (SHRI 
TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) The Comprehensive Policy Package for the Small 
Scale Industries and Tiny Sector was announced on 30th August, 2000 
which aims to ensure enhanced fiscal and credit support, better 
infrastructural and marketing facilities and incentives for technology 
upgradation. Some of the significant measures included in the policy 
package and those taken during last 4 years to develop and boost the 
SSIs are:— 
(i) Raising the excise exemption limit for SSis on first clearances 
of Rs. 50 lakhs to Rs. 100 lakhs, on annual turnover upto 
Rs. 300 lakhs. 
(ii) Launching of Cr edit Guarantee Fund Scheme for providing 
collateral free loans upto Rs. 25 lakhs. 
(iii)   Raising the composite loan  limit from Rs. 10 lakhs to 
Rs.25 lakhs. 
199 

RAJYA SABHA [14 August, 2003] 
(iv) Launching of Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme for 
technology upgradation providing 12% capital subsidy for 
technology upgradation in selected sub-sectors. 
(v) Enhancing the Project cost limit upto Rs. 50 lakhs under 
National Equity Fund Scheme. 
(vi) A new Market Development Assistance (MDA) Scheme 
launched providing financial assistance from participating in 
international fairs, exhibitions and reimbursement of expenses 
incurred on adopting Bar-coding by EAN India. 
(vii) Extending ISO 9000 Certification Reimbursement Scheme to 
Tenth Five Year Plan and also providing assistance for acquiring 
ISO 14000 Certification. 
(viii) Providing financial assistance to SSI Associations for setting 
up of testing facilities; 
(ix) The modified Integrated Infrastructural Development (IID) 
Scheme to provide for 50% reservation for rural areas and 
50% for tiny units. 
(x) Issuance of revised guidelines by Reserve Bank of India for 
rehabilitation of sick SSI units and revival of potentially viable 
units, based on Kohli Committee recommendations. 
(xi) In addition, earlier incentives and Schemes for enhancing flow 
of credit, technology upgradation, marketing promotion, etc. 
are being continued. 
(b) The estimated number of persons employed in the SSI Sector

Mission to Moon 
2694. SHRIB. J. PANDA: 
MISS MABEL REBELLO: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state : 
(a) whether ISRO has planned a mission around the orbit of Moon 
by the year 2007; 
(b) whether certain foreign countries have evinced interest to join 
this mission, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the areas where the space research is being focussed; and 
(d) whether the country possess a la unch vehicle capability for the 
purpose? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SPACE (SHRI 
SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) An Unmanned Moon Mission has 
been planned for 2008-09. 
(b) Yes, Sir. Interest has been shown by the European Space Agency 
(ESA) and Canadian Space Agency (C SA). However, details have not 
yet been worked out. 
(c) It is proposed to carry out high-resolution remote sensing of the 
Moon in visible, near infrared, low energy x-rays and high energy x-ray 
regions. This would enable us to study the origin and chemical evolution 
of the moon, its geological features , impact phenomena, survey of its 
precious resources such as Helium -Thr ee, which is considered to be a 
potential source of cleanest energy, with minimum residual radio-activity. 
(d) Yes, Sir. It is proposed to use the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle 
(PSLV) for the Mission. 
Unmanned spaceship to Moon 
2695. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: 
SHRI RAJEEVSHUKLA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state : 
203 

RAJYASABHA [14 August, 2003] 
(a) whether it is a  fact that Government propose to launch an 
unmanned spaceship to moon; 
(b) if so, the purpose and the cost involved in this venture; and 
(c) what is the urgency for such a venture when a lot of developmental 
activities are held up for want of funds and what public interest and 
removal of poverty are going to be served by such a venture? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF SPACE (SHRI 
SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) In consonance with the mandate of 
Indian Space Research Organisation for research in space sciences and 
based on the interest of the scien tific community, an unmanned spacecraft 
mission around moon has been planned. 
(b) The main purpose of the mission is to study the hitherto unexplored 
aspects of the moon and to expand the horizon of our scientific knowledge 
and also to upgrade our technological capability. The cost of the mission 
is presently estimated to be Rs. 386.00 crores. 
(c) Such a deep space mission would throw-up challenges to our 
vision and scientific knowledge and upgrade our technological capabilities. 
Moon can be the outpost for furt her planetary exploration. The 
technological up-gradation involved in this mission would provide several 
spin-offs in the areas of minera l prospecting, power generation, 
communication systems, etc.

Recycling and better management of plastic waste 
SHRI PARMESHWAR KUMAR AGARWALLA (Jharkhand): Madam, 
the plastic industry in India contribu tes more than two million tonnes of 
plastic to our waste stream. These include bottles, food packagings, 
cement bags, medical disposals, all of  which become waste with just one 
use. This industry is growing at 12-15 per cent annually. It is good that the 
industry is growing, because of wh ich the employment opportunities are 
increasing, so also the GDP. But at what cost? The whole country, the 
entire landscape, is being littered with plastic bottles and thin plastic bags. 
They keep flying everywhere causing eye-sores to many people. Actually it 
is not the use of plastic that is caus ing the problem, but the indiscriminate 
waste that is being created which ha s become a matter of serious concern 
for the environment. It is true that the plastic has changed our lives, and it 
is affordable even to a poor man. But the waste is choking the animals, 
including the cow, and the soil. T here is no waste management of the 
plastic waste in our country. People are not habituated to properly throw 
away the used plastic things including bottles and bags. The Government 
has banned the manufacture of thin plastic bags. But this alone is not 
sufficient. 
In many Western countries including Sweden, Norway and Germany, 
the plastic manufacturers are forced to collect plastic waste and recycle it. 
The European Union says, "The producers are responsible". Management 
of waste plastic and recycling of it ar e essential now in our country. Unless 
these things are done, the problem cannot be solved. It is difficult to stop 
manufacture of plastic altogether, but waste management and recycling are 
very well in our hands. The Government should, therefore, take necessary 
steps for recycling of the plastic waste and better management of the 
plastic waste.

SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO (Andhra Pradesh): Madam, the 
Government of Andhra Pradesh, with the objective of universalisation of 
elementary education, is implementing the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, and 
giving hot, cooked food to the children of I-VII standards in the Government 
schools, local bodies' schools and the Government-aided primary and 
upper-primary schools in Andhra Pradesh; the Scheme has a coverage of 
74.59 lakh children in the year 20 02-03. The implementation agencies for 
this scheme are the DWCRA, the Co mmunity Development Agencies, the 
NGOs, etc. The State Government has  also provided funds to all the 
District Collectors for the construction of additional rooms in schools to be 
used as kitchens. The Government is al so ensuring provision of 300 calories 
and 8-12 grams of protein content per child everyday, with boiled eggs and 
bananas once in a week. Apart from this, the Government is thinking of 
introducing two more recipes -- hot pongal and tomato bhat - very shortly. 
The cost of it comes to Re.1 and Rs.1.10 respectively per child, which is far 
more than 0.5 paise spent by many other States. All these things have 
been substantiated by a survey conduc ted by the Centre for Development

number of kitchens running  on  gas is 48,056 and the total  number of

Need to review the guidelines of Prime Minister's Rojgar Yojana 
SHRI C. PERUMAL (Tamil Nadu): Madam Deputy Chairperson, the 
Prime Minister's Rojgar Yojana was launched to help the unemployed youth 
to set up self-employment ventures. This scheme is specially meant for the 
educated unemployed who constitute 40 per cent of the unemployed 
people. There are clear guidelines in re spect of sanction of loans under the 
Prime Minister's Rojgar Yojana. But, the nationalised banks do not observe 
these guidelines. The banks have unwritten rules and find ways to refuse 
loan to the unemployed youth who approach them. One of the salient 
features of this scheme is the wa iving the collateral security. The 
matriculation certificate of the person  applying for loan is the guarantee 
required under the guidelines. For se lf-employment projects up to rupees 
one lakh, no collateral security is required. But, the banks do not follow 
these guidelines. As a result, the poor unemployed youth are not able to get 
the benefit of the scheme.  I request the Government to issue firm directive 
to all the nationalised banks to sanction loans without asking for security. 
The requirement of collateral security for loans above rupees one lakh 
should also be waived. Otherwise, the very purpose of this scheme will be 
defeated. Since the trend of higher gr owth of unemployment of educated 
youth continues, it is necessary to see that the Prime Minister's Rojgar 
Yojana is implemented in letter and spirit. Therefore, the Government should 
review the guidelines and direct the banks to sanction loans on the basis of 
matriculation certificate of  the applicant, without the requirement of any form 
of security. Such a step alone will achieve the target, as spelt out in the 
scheme. Thank you, Madam.
